newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish deputy PM calls for journalists' release.
newsitem.headline: Turkish deputy PM calls for journalists' release.

text.p: Turkish Deputy Prime Minister Bulent Ecevit called on Monday for the release of writers and journalists held in Turkish prisons and an end to torture, state-run Anatolian news agency said.

"The first step is the release of journalists and writers in jail ... We will take firm steps to end the practice of beatings and torture, especially against journalists," Ecevit told a visiting delegation of Western reporters, the agency said.
The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) delegation was led by Terry Anderson, a former Associated Press reporter held hostage in Lebanon for seven years.
The group's visit, aimed at seeking the release of jailed journalists, comes two weeks after the appointment of a right-left coalition including leftist Ecevit.
On Wednesday, the group is to visit jailed editor Ocak Isik Yurtcu, now in the third year of an almost 16-year sentence. The CPJ last November gave Yurtcu its International Press Freedom award.
Asked by Anderson about a possible early release of Yurtcu, Ecevit said: "This will be resolved by the end of July."
At least 78 journalists are jailed in Turkey over charges connected with their work, according to CPJ figures.

Most are imprisoned under Turkey's anti-terrorism laws for spreading "separatist propaganda" in reporting the insurgency by Kurdish rebels seeking self-rule in the southeast of the country. More than 25,000 people have died in the conflict.
